title: Climbing Stairs
prompt: Given n stairs, you can climb either 1 or 2 stairs at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

spec.input: An integer n, the number of stairs.
spec.output: Return the number of distinct ways to reach stair n when every move is either 1 or 2 stairs.
examples: There are 8 valid sequences of 1-step and 2-step moves.

title: Frog Jump
prompt: A frog starts at the first stair and wants to reach the last. From stair i it can jump to i+1 or i+2. The energy cost of a jump is the absolute difference in heights. Find the minimum energy.

spec.input: An integer array `heights`; the frog starts at index 0.
spec.output: Return the minimum total energy needed to reach the last index. A jump of 1 or 2 positions costs the absolute height difference.
examples: Choose jumps that minimize the accumulated height difference.

title: Frog Jump with K Distance
prompt: The frog can jump from stair i to any of the next k stairs. The cost is the absolute difference between the two heights. Find the minimum energy needed to reach the last stair.

spec.input: An array `heights` and maximum jump distance `k`.
spec.output: Return the minimum energy needed to reach the last index. From i, jump to any index i+1 … i+k.
spec.constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 10^4; 1 ≤ k ≤ n; heights are non-negative

title: Maximum Sum of Non-Adjacent Elements
prompt: Given an array of integers, choose a subset with no two chosen elements adjacent and maximize the sum.

spec.input: An integer array `nums`.
spec.output: Return the maximum sum obtainable by selecting elements so that no two selected indices are adjacent.

title: House Robber 2
prompt: Houses are arranged in a circle. Robbing adjacent houses is forbidden. Find the maximum amount that can be robbed.

spec.input: An array `nums` representing money in houses arranged in a circle.
spec.output: Return the maximum amount that can be robbed without robbing two adjacent houses. The first and last houses are also adjacent.

title: Ninja's Training
prompt: For n days, choose one of three activities per day. Each activity gives points, but you cannot choose the same activity on consecutive days. Maximize total points.

spec.input: An n×3 array `points`, where points[d][a] is the score from doing activity a on day d.
spec.output: Return the maximum total score if the same activity cannot be chosen on consecutive days.
examples: Choose activity 2, then 2 is forbidden on the next day, so choose another optimal activity, continuing accordingly.

title: Grid Unique Paths
prompt: Count the number of ways to move from the top-left to the bottom-right of an m x n grid when you can only move right or down.

spec.input: Grid dimensions m and n.
spec.output: Return the number of ways to move from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell using only right and down moves.
examples: There are three paths through a 3-row × 2-column grid.
Choose positions of the two down moves among eight total moves.

title: Unique Paths 2
prompt: Count paths through a grid with obstacles. You may move only right or down, and blocked cells cannot be visited.

spec.input: An m×n binary grid; 1 denotes an obstacle and 0 denotes a free cell.
spec.output: Return the number of valid top-left to bottom-right paths moving only right or down.
examples: The center obstacle blocks paths through the middle.

title: Minimum Path Sum in Grid
prompt: Given a grid of non-negative numbers, move only right or down from top-left to bottom-right and minimize the sum of visited cells.

spec.input: An m×n grid of non-negative costs.
spec.output: Return the minimum cost of a path from the top-left to bottom-right, moving only right or down.

title: Triangle
prompt: Given a triangle of numbers, start at the top and move to adjacent numbers on the next row. Find the minimum path sum to the bottom.

spec.input: A triangular array; row i contains i+1 values.
spec.output: Return the minimum top-to-bottom path sum. From position j, move to j or j+1 in the next row.

title: Minimum/Maximum Falling Path Sum
prompt: In a square matrix, start in any top-row cell and move to the next row by down-left, down, or down-right. Find the minimum falling path sum.

spec.input: An n×n matrix of integers.
spec.output: Return the minimum sum of a falling path from the first row to the last. From column c, move to c-1, c, or c+1 in the next row.

title: Cherry Pickup II
prompt: Two robots start in the first row of a grid at the leftmost and rightmost columns. Each moves down-left, down, or down-right. Maximize total cherries collected; a cell counts once if both robots occupy it.

spec.input: An r×c grid of non-negative cherries. Robot A starts at (0,0); Robot B starts at (0,c-1).
spec.output: Return the maximum cherries collected while both robots move to the last row. Each step changes a robot's column by -1, 0, or +1. A cell counts once if both robots share it.
examples: The robots coordinate their paths to maximize distinct collected cherries.

title: Subset Sum Equals to Target
prompt: Given an array and a target, determine whether some subset of the array has sum exactly equal to the target.

spec.input: An array of non-negative integers and a target sum.
spec.output: Return True if some subset of the array sums exactly to target; otherwise False.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
prompt: Determine whether an array can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum.

spec.input: An array of positive integers.
spec.output: Return True when the array can be divided into two subsets with equal sum.
examples: The array can be split as [1,5,5] and [11].

title: Partition A Set Into Two Subsets With Minimum Absolute Sum Difference
prompt: Partition the array into two subsets so that the absolute difference of their sums is as small as possible. Return that minimum difference.

spec.input: An array of non-negative integers.
spec.output: Split all elements into two subsets and minimize the absolute difference between their sums.
examples: For example, 8+5 versus 6 gives difference 7; the optimum is 3.

title: Count Subsets with Sum K
prompt: Count the number of subsets whose elements sum exactly to K. Handle zeros correctly.

spec.input: An array of non-negative integers and a target sum k.
spec.output: Return the number of subsets whose elements add up exactly to k.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200; 0 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^4; return the exact count or apply the platform's required modulus.
examples: Every selection of the two zeros can accompany the 1.

title: Count Partitions With Given Difference
prompt: Count partitions of the array into two subsets whose sum difference equals a given target difference.

spec.input: An array of non-negative integers and an integer difference diff.
spec.output: Count partitions into two subsets S1 and S2 such that sum(S1) - sum(S2) = diff.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200; 0 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100; use the modulus specified by your chosen judge if needed.
examples: There are three valid assignments of the elements to the two subsets.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
prompt: Given n items with weights and values and a knapsack capacity, choose each item at most once to maximize total value without exceeding capacity.

spec.format: Function signature: `def knapsack_01(weights, values, capacity) -> int`
spec.input: n items with a weight and value for each item, plus a knapsack capacity. Each item may be chosen at most once.
spec.output: Return the maximum value whose total weight does not exceed capacity.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1,000; 1 ≤ weights[i] ≤ capacity ≤ 10^4; values are non-negative

title: Minimum Coins
prompt: Given coin denominations with unlimited supply and a target amount, return the minimum number of coins needed, or -1 if impossible.

spec.input: Coin denominations `coins` and a target amount. Each denomination can be used unlimited times.
spec.output: Return the minimum number of coins needed to make amount, or -1 when it is impossible.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ len(coins) ≤ 20; 0 ≤ amount ≤ 10^4; coin values are positive

title: Target Sum
prompt: Assign either + or - to every number so that the resulting expression equals a target. Count the number of valid assignments.

spec.input: A list of non-negative integers. Put either '+' or '-' before every element.
spec.output: Return how many sign assignments evaluate to target.
examples: The only possible results are +1 and -1.

title: Coin Change 2
prompt: Given unlimited coins and an amount, count the number of combinations that make the amount. Order does not matter.

spec.input: Coin denominations with unlimited supply and a target amount.
spec.output: Return the number of distinct combinations that make amount; different orders of the same coins count once.

title: Unbounded Knapsack
prompt: Given item weights and values with unlimited copies, maximize value without exceeding the knapsack capacity.

spec.format: Function signature: `def unbounded_knapsack(weights, values, capacity) -> int`
spec.input: Item weights and values with unlimited copies allowed, plus capacity.
spec.output: Return the maximum value that fits within capacity.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1,000; weights are positive and values are non-negative
examples: Take the weight-2 item five times.

title: Rod Cutting Problem
prompt: Given prices for rod pieces of every length, cut a rod of length n to maximize the total obtainable price. Each length can be used multiple times.

spec.input: An array `price` where price[i-1] is the selling price of a rod piece of length i, plus total rod length n.
spec.output: Return the maximum revenue obtainable by cutting the rod into pieces of integer lengths.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
prompt: Given two strings, find the length of their longest common subsequence while preserving character order.

spec.input: Two strings a and b.
spec.output: Return the length of their longest common subsequence.

title: Print Longest Common Subsequence
prompt: Given two strings, construct and return one longest common subsequence, not only its length.

spec.input: Two strings a and b.
spec.output: Return any one longest common subsequence of a and b.

title: Longest Common Substring
prompt: Given two strings, find the maximum length of a contiguous substring appearing in both strings.

spec.input: Two strings a and b.
spec.output: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring occurring in both strings.
examples: "jkl" is not fully present; the longest common contiguous match has length 2 in this example.

title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
prompt: Find the length of the longest subsequence of a string that reads the same forward and backward.

spec.input: A string s.
spec.output: Return the length of its longest palindromic subsequence.

title: Minimum Insertions to Make String Palindrome
prompt: Return the minimum number of insertions needed to turn a string into a palindrome.

spec.input: A string s.
spec.output: Return the minimum number of character insertions needed to make s a palindrome.
examples: For example, insert characters to obtain a palindrome such as "mbdadbm".

title: Minimum Insertions/Deletions to Convert String A to String B
prompt: Find the minimum number of insertions and deletions required to transform string A into string B.

spec.input: Two strings a and b.
spec.output: Return the minimum number of insertions plus deletions needed to transform a into b. Substitution is not allowed.
examples: Delete h, delete one extra character, and insert p/e as needed; the optimum is 3.

title: Shortest Common Supersequence
prompt: Return the shortest string that contains both input strings as subsequences.

spec.input: Two strings a and b.
spec.output: Return any shortest string that contains both a and b as subsequences.

title: Distinct Subsequences
prompt: Given strings s and t, count how many distinct subsequences of s equal t.

spec.input: Two strings s and t.
spec.output: Count how many distinct subsequences of s are exactly equal to t.
examples: There are three ways to delete one of the repeated b characters.
There are five distinct index selections producing bag.

title: Edit Distance
prompt: Find the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and substitutions required to transform one string into another.

spec.input: Two strings a and b.
spec.output: Return the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, or replacements needed to transform a into b.
examples: One optimal sequence has three edits.
The classic minimum edit distance is 5.

title: Wildcard Matching
prompt: Match a text against a pattern where '?' matches one character and '*' matches any sequence of characters.

spec.input: A text s and pattern p. '?' matches exactly one character; '*' matches any sequence, including empty.
spec.output: Return True if the whole text matches the whole pattern.
examples: The pattern matches only one character.
The second character does not match a.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
prompt: Given daily stock prices, make at most one buy and one sell. Return the maximum profit.

spec.input: Daily stock prices.
spec.output: Choose one buy day before one sell day and maximize profit. You may also make no transaction.
examples: Prices only fall, so do nothing.

title: Buy and Sell Stock II
prompt: You may complete unlimited buy/sell transactions, but must sell before buying again. Maximize profit.

spec.input: Daily stock prices. You may make as many complete buy/sell transactions as you like, holding at most one share.
spec.output: Return the maximum total profit.
examples: Buy once at 1 and sell at 5, or accumulate equivalent rises.

title: Buy and Sell Stocks III
prompt: You may complete at most two transactions. Maximize profit.

spec.input: Daily prices; at most two complete transactions are allowed.
spec.output: Return the maximum achievable profit.
examples: Only one profitable run is needed.

title: Buy and Stock Sell IV
prompt: You may complete at most k transactions. Maximize profit.

spec.input: Daily prices and a maximum number k of complete transactions.
spec.output: Return the maximum profit with at most k buy→sell pairs.

title: Buy and Sell Stocks With Cooldown
prompt: After selling a stock, you must wait one day before buying again. Maximize profit.

spec.input: Daily prices. After selling, one full day must pass before another purchase.
spec.output: Return the maximum profit with unlimited transactions under the cooldown rule.

title: Buy and Sell Stocks With Transaction Fee
prompt: Each completed transaction incurs a fixed fee. You may trade multiple times. Maximize profit.

spec.input: Daily prices and a fixed transaction fee charged whenever a share is sold.
spec.output: Return the maximum profit with unlimited transactions.
examples: Two profitable moves remain after fees.
The fee makes the trade unprofitable.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
prompt: Given an array, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

spec.input: An integer array.
spec.output: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 2,500 for O(n²) DP; values fit 32-bit signed integers

title: Printing Longest Increasing Subsequence
prompt: Given an array, output one longest strictly increasing subsequence, not just its length.

spec.input: An integer array.
spec.output: Return any one longest strictly increasing subsequence.
examples: Strict increase means only one element can be selected.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence — Binary Search
prompt: Solve LIS using the O(n log n) tails/binary-search technique and return its length.

spec.input: An integer array.
spec.output: Return the LIS length using the tails + binary-search method.
examples: One optimal increasing subsequence has length 6.

title: Largest Divisible Subset
prompt: Given distinct positive integers, find the largest subset such that for every pair, one number divides the other.

spec.input: Distinct positive integers.
spec.output: Return any largest subset where for every pair a,b, either a divides b or b divides a.

title: Longest String Chain
prompt: Find the longest chain of words where each next word can be formed by inserting exactly one character into the previous word.

spec.input: A list of unique lowercase words.
spec.output: Return the maximum chain length where each next word can be created by inserting exactly one character into the previous word.
examples: The words can form a chain of length 5.

title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence
prompt: Find the longest subsequence that first strictly increases and then strictly decreases.

spec.input: An integer array.
spec.output: Return the length of a subsequence that strictly increases and then strictly decreases. A purely increasing/decreasing subsequence is allowed when it fits the definition.
examples: The whole sequence increases then decreases.
An optimal bitonic subsequence has length 6.

title: Number of Longest Increasing Subsequences
prompt: Count how many distinct subsequences have the maximum possible strictly increasing length.

spec.input: An integer array.
spec.output: Count the number of strictly increasing subsequences having maximum possible length.
examples: The longest length is 4, ending with 5,7 or 4,7.
The longest length is 1 and each position forms one LIS.

title: Matrix Chain Multiplication
prompt: Given matrix dimensions, determine the minimum number of scalar multiplications required to multiply the whole matrix chain.

spec.input: An array `dims` of length n+1 where matrix i has dimensions dims[i-1] × dims[i].
spec.output: Return the minimum number of scalar multiplications needed to multiply the entire chain.

title: Matrix Chain Multiplication — Bottom-Up
prompt: Implement matrix-chain multiplication with bottom-up tabulation and return the minimum multiplication cost.

spec.input: The same matrix-dimension array as DP 48.
spec.output: Return the minimum scalar multiplication count, implemented with bottom-up interval DP.
examples: Bottom-up interval DP should produce the same optimum.
The best multiplication order minimizes intermediate matrix sizes.

title: Minimum Cost to Cut the Stick
prompt: A stick of given length is cut at specified positions. Each cut costs the current stick length. Find the minimum total cost.

spec.input: A stick of length `length` and distinct cut positions inside it.
spec.output: Perform all cuts. A cut costs the length of the current stick segment being cut. Return the minimum total cost.
examples: An optimal cutting order gives total cost 16.
Reordering the cuts changes the total cost; minimize it.

title: Burst Balloons
prompt: Burst balloons in an order that maximizes coins. Bursting i earns nums[left] * nums[i] * nums[right] for its current neighbours.

spec.input: An array of positive balloon values. When balloon i is burst, its coins equal left_value * nums[i] * right_value among balloons still present.
spec.output: Burst every balloon in an order that maximizes total coins.
examples: An optimal bursting order earns 167 coins.

title: Evaluate Boolean Expression to True
prompt: Count the number of ways to parenthesize a boolean expression so that it evaluates to true.

spec.input: A boolean expression with operands T/F and binary operators &, |, ^. Parenthesize it in different valid ways.
spec.output: Return the number of parenthesizations whose value is True.
spec.constraints: Odd expression length; number of operands ≤ 200. Apply the modulus required by your judge if specified.
examples: Different parenthesizations can change precedence; count those evaluating to True.
The single operand is already True.

title: Palindrome Partitioning II
prompt: Partition a string into palindromic substrings using the minimum possible number of cuts.

spec.input: A string s.
spec.output: Partition s into palindromic substrings using the minimum number of cuts. Return that minimum.
examples: A one-character string needs no cut.

title: Partition Array for Maximum Sum
prompt: Partition an array into contiguous groups of length at most k. A group's contribution is its length multiplied by its maximum element. Maximize the total.

spec.input: An array arr and an integer k. Partition arr into contiguous blocks, each of length at most k.
spec.output: For every block, contribution = block length × maximum element in that block. Maximize the sum of all block contributions.
spec.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 500; 1 ≤ k ≤ n; values may be negative depending on the judge
examples: Choose blocks to maximize each block's max×length contribution.

title: Maximum Rectangle Area with all 1's
prompt: Given a binary matrix, find the area of the largest rectangle containing only 1s.

spec.input: A binary matrix containing '0' and '1' values.
spec.output: Return the area of the largest axis-aligned rectangle containing only 1s.

title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
prompt: Given a binary matrix, count all square submatrices consisting entirely of 1s.

spec.input: A binary matrix containing 0 and 1.
spec.output: Count every square submatrix whose cells are all 1.
